scenario: [LGRA.9.6.1] / [LGRA.9.7.1]: a literal is a primary, so a bare literal takes a member suffix with no parentheses. No literal's type has a member a program can call: DS reads no temporal text ([LTIM.14]), and a `String` has no member. So the suffix is shown parsed by the refusal it reaches: `"abc".to_time("iso8601")` is DS_VALIDATE_UNKNOWN_MEMBER, which only a parsed member call can raise; a parser that gave a bare literal no suffix refuses with DS_PARSE_GENERIC at the `.`. The companion LGRA.9.6.1_literal_takes_a_suffix pins the two casts. PATH PINNED: `dsc.parse.lgra_9_6_1_postfix` building the member call on the string primary, and `dsc.typecheck.member_call_type`'s `unknown_member`.
rules_ds:
schema S scope logical:
    entity_id: String key

rule r:
    S where now() > "abc".to_time("iso8601")
->
    log info "x"
